main_body: Japanese-style two-tier building: a large blue-grey tile roof with ridge cap, a cream plaster band with slit windows, a small lower roof, and a wooden lattice front with a dark doorway and straw heaps.
top_band: Ridge cap rows 1-5 (L130-158), then the tile roof slope rows 6-29 (L56-158, a mid-dark tile surface) under the outline row 0; a dark eave row at 30-32 separates it from the cream plaster wall (L221, rows 33-40)
evidence: The column at x=32 meets the ridge cap, then a big tiled roof slope that reads as a surface seen from above. A dark eave shadow (rows 30-32) follows, then the vertical plaster wall (rows 33-40). A second small roof slope sits at rows 41-47, with a lattice front and an inset dark doorway below it. The roofs show top slopes and the walls are separate vertical faces, as in the house references, so the 3/4 contract is met.

style.evidence: The roof has about 4-5 blue-grey tones with a tile-stripe pattern, which is decent. The plaster band and the dark doorway are nearly flat, and the lattice is a repetitive 2-3 tone pattern. Measured facts are well below both references: 34 distinct colours against 66 and 185, and a median of 8 colours per tile against 11 and 18. Dark edge pixels are 72% near-neutral against 7-9% for the references, so the outline leans sticker-like black rather than a tinted material tone. Beside the references it looks thinner and flatter.
